automation_evidence.quote:
first LLM, LLM-Agent, uses these forecasts to make fine grained
traffic signal control, while the second LLM, LLM-Critic, refines LLM-Agent’s outputs, correcting errors and hallucinations.

metric_evidence.quote:
HeraldLight achieves a 20.03% reduction in average travel
time relative to SOTA method.

evidence.quote:
Hallucination is defined as context-incoherent, repetitive, or
constraint-violating outputs at the decision step. The metric
is computed as the fraction of interactions that exhibit any
such symptoms.

practical_problems.note: LLM decision hallucination rate (Agent vs Agent+Critic) on Hangzhou 2; not a time series obstacle proper calibration: agent-internal decision hallucination, not a time series obstacle

summary: Herald queue forecasts plus an LLM agent and critic automate signal-phase timing and cut average travel time versus baselines in CityFlow simulation; hallucination rate with and without the critic is also measured.
